marks.gloss_en: שהרי אמרה תורה: ואל אשה בנדת טומאתה לא תקרב
the widow: my husband, who studied much, read much and served scholars much -- why did he die at half his days?
and these are among the halakhot they said in the upper storey of Chananya ben Chizkiya ben Garon
שנאמר: אך בשרו עליו יכאב ונפשו עליו תאבל (Job 14:22)
איני?! והאמר רב יצחק: קשה רימה למת כמחט בבשר החי -- is that so? did not Rav Yitzchak say the worm is as hard to the dead as a needle to living flesh?
אימא: אין בשר המת שבחי מרגיש באיזמל -- say rather: the dead flesh in the living does not feel the scalpel (= p_basar_met_shebachai; an emendation of the wording)
alternatively: the flesh of the dead does not feel the scalpel
RSBG: we too hold the troubles dear
alternatively: a fool is not hurt
truly, that man is remembered for good, and Chananya ben Chizkiya is his name
these disqualify teruma: one who eats first-degree food, and one who eats second-degree food
תא שמע: אין פולין לאור הנר ואין קורין לאור הנר, ואלו מן ההלכות שאמרו בעליית חנניה -- the list calls rulings already stated 'among the halakhot of the upper storey', so 'and these' points back
we learned 'and these' -- [referring to] the ones we have said
who wrote Megillat Ta'anit? They said: Chananya ben Chizkiya and his faction, who cherished the troubles
